samples.identification: Lumina Celestia data-availability node source, workspace version 1.3.0
samples.marker_line: Lumina: Celestia node source; build and test network tooling
evidence: cli/src/main.rs enters lumina_cli::run; common.rs dispatches the explicitly selected native Node or browser server operation.
cli/src/native.rs builds a node with configured network, bootnodes and Redb or in-memory stores, then reports synchronization events.
node/src/utils/dns.rs fetches DNS-over-HTTPS TXT answers and accepts bootnode multiaddresses with the expected peer ID; the response is network configuration, not executed code.
proto/build.rs compiles vendored protobuf descriptors through protox and prost/tonic and applies generated type attributes.
The pull_request_target workflow validates PR titles with a pinned action and read-only pull-request permission; it does not check out or execute the PR head.
Release secrets are used for the documented GitHub/npm/Cargo publication paths. CI credentials belong to the disposable private test network.
The highest-scored XML member is an Android demo manifest with INTERNET permission and an exported launcher activity. Node.kt presents network-selection buttons and starts the selected Lumina node.
The .oss-scanner Dockerfile verifies downloaded development binaries using SHA-256. Its launcher starts private local services and cleans up its own processes and temporary state.
samples.provenance: Repository and version are self-declared in the archive; this mutable main-branch snapshot was not independently byte-verified against upstream.
samples.missing_context: No deployed binary, operator command line, or host telemetry was supplied. Verdict addresses the supplied source archive.

samples.identification: Microsoft Programming Experience Toolkit / MakeCode pxt-core 0.19.5
samples.marker_line: Microsoft PXT 0.19.5: MakeCode tools; legitimate WinRT grant
evidence: package.json identifies pxt-core 0.19.5, with CLI, compiler, simulator, Blockly and Monaco development components.
cli/nodeutil.ts spawns configured build tools; cli/cli.ts retrieves and updates credentials under the application-specific pxt target namespace for explicit login and publication operations.
The local development server defaults to localhost, checks an authorization token for local APIs, and uses token-bearing WebSocket paths for serial/debug/HID access.
external/tdast.js contains transpiled TouchDevelop compiler/runtime code. CompiledScript.init and reinit evaluate supplied compiled program text and invoke it as part of the program runtime.

pxtwinrt/deploy.ts writes compiled firmware to matching removable-device folders or a user-selected save location; other WinRT modules support serial/HID device interaction and application project storage.
Four manifest members actually include HTTP/HTTPS origins with WindowsRuntimeAccess=all. The suspicious unrestricted-WinRT declaration is accurate and remains unchanged.
samples.provenance: Forager fetched pkg:golang/github.com/microsoft/pxt@v0.19.5 from proxy.golang.org, verified the module through sum.golang.org, and recovered the exact supplied SHA-256.
samples.missing_context: The historical hosted origins and any installed application state were not supplied. Broad remote WinRT authority is real risk, but the supplied code supports MakeCode device integration rather than theft or a backdoor.

samples.marker_line: Craft iOS 0.0.330: opt-in native APIs; add capability coverage
evidence: package.json has no install lifecycle hook. dist/index.js exports builder functions; dist/cli.js dispatches explicit init/build/open/run/audit-sources commands.

build reads the project configuration, copies assets, generates Xcode settings and invokes xcodegen. run invokes Xcode and Simulator tooling. postGenerate uses a configured executable and argument array through Bun.spawnSync.
Native functionality is represented by Swift templates and configuration feature flags. The main page dispatcher checks an origin allowlist; chrome/hybrid relays additionally check the main frame.
CraftVoiceRecording.swift checks the active requesting screen, requests microphone permission, creates a bounded-duration recorder and stops/cleans it when backgrounded or cancelled.
CraftNativeFiles.swift restricts multipart-upload reads and deletion to files owned beneath its temporary file root. Image input uses a picker or a feature-gated camera.
CraftCrashReporter.swift activates only with configured crashReporting settings and a nonempty project key; it queues application crash/session reports for the configured host or bughq.org.

CraftNativeScreen.swift reads bundled runtime/screen JavaScript, decompresses gzip assets with a size bound and evaluates them through JavaScriptCore. CraftApp.swift evaluates bridge/UI code through WebKit.
CryptoKit SHA-256/SHA-512 and SecRandomCopyBytes provide hashes and random bytes for application functions. These operations and zlib inflate were missing from existing Swift match scopes.
samples.provenance: Forager recovered the exact supplied SHA-256 from the npm registry for pkg:npm/@craft-native/ios@0.0.330.
samples.missing_context: No consuming project configuration, generated app, or deployed JavaScript bundle was supplied. The package is a configurable builder; a separately supplied application could use its capabilities differently.

comparison_method: Local, slow atomscan scans with updates disabled and --follow=none compare original archive members independently of fetch-budget variation. Initial and repeated dependency/reference-aware scans were also reviewed.

rule_changes.added: Six notable definitions: two parsed method-call observations, two framework-qualified native JavaScript bridge composites, and two AVFoundation recording API traits.
rule_changes.extended: Retain existing SHA-256, SHA-512, SecRandomCopyBytes and zlib inflate observations and add Swift/iOS coverage. SHA-256 additionally recognizes the CryptoKit .hash method spelling.
rule_changes.placement: Native interpreter bridge invocations use eval/indirect, whose taxonomy contract includes bridges. Method names without framework context remain syntax observations. Recording, hashes, randomness and decompression retain their resource/operation homes.
rule_changes.preserved: All original archive findings, including the suspicious AppX WinRT grant, are retained.

dependency_comparison.lumina: No lost findings in the repeated dependency-aware scan.
dependency_comparison.pxt: The fetch budget skipped two previously fetched immutable GitHub assets: sgn-de0af0b55144d4f4.js and aria-live-e0f60f15396869e3.js. Forager recovered their original hashes and isolated atomscan scans retained all their notable findings; the standalone rendering emitted fewer baseline/component context findings. No hostile/suspicious or notable attack coverage was lost.
dependency_comparison.pxt_root_unique_hostile_suspicious: 0/1 before and after, including fetched references; four original manifest members retain the suspicious trait.

verification.focused_controls: Passed: actual native calls match; comments, type annotations and declarations do not; unrelated evaluate methods retain syntax observations without interpreter capability claims.
verification.classifier_disagreement: All three root ML probability values remain 1.0 at level 0 (HOSTILE) before and after. Concrete execution paths support BENIGN. No inaccurate severity changes or duplicate hostile rules were added to influence the classifier.
verification.analysis_limits: Static review only. Atomscan reported flow-analysis limits in some bundles/templates and a v18/v21 feature-spec mismatch. Manual source tracing supplies the behavioral reasoning; no runtime success is inferred.
